newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan not worried over Gecamines cobalt supply.
newsitem.headline: Japan not worried over Gecamines cobalt supply.

text.p: Japanese traders said on Thursday they were not worried that Gecamines might not be able to deliver cobalt supplies agreed upon under long-term contracts, despite an expected decline in its output in 1997.
"Better products are getting more and more difficult to come by," said a trader. "But we understand the situation is improving. So we're hoping for the best."
Traders in Tokyo said they had not seen term contracts being unfulfilled or shipments being delayed so far.
Yet they said they were not signing new contracts which would involve large-quantity cobalt shipments from Gecamines.

Gecamines chairman Mbaka Kawaya told Reuters in Mauritius on Wednesday that Congo's state mining company expected 1997 cobalt output to drop from about 4,000 tonnes in 1996 before increasing next year.
Kawaya also said Gecamines had stockpiles of two months worth of cobalt production, or about 670 tonnes.
This prompted some worries in London overnight that Gecamines could not satisfy demand for cobalt under the long-term contracts, most of which centre on Japan.
A Tokyo source with close contacts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly Zaire, said it was difficult to gauge the stockpile figure without further details.

The source estimated Gecamines' stockpiles totalled about 4,000 tonnes at the end of 1996, including stocks at its agents around the world, ports and banks. Some banks held cobalt stockpiles as collateral for their lending to Gecamines, the source said.
A report by Mitsui & Co Ltd shows Japan imported 5,700 tonnes of cobalt last year, with Congo accounting for 1,533 tonnes of the total.
Traders estimated about one-third of Japan's cobalt imports from Gecamines were based on term contracts.
